notes: Watched against Codex 0.171 in tmux on 2026-11-23: an escalated command's approval, a Plan-mode question (request_user_input), a turn running and the prompt after it; the screens are `testdata/screens/codex-*`. The title is the strongest signal: Codex writes `Action Required` into it whenever it waits on the person, and its own spinner frame in front of the session name otherwise.

rules.note: Codex titles the terminal `[ ! ] Action Required | <prompt> | <folder>` both while an approval is open and while a question is; the question screen also says `esc to interrupt`, so without the title it reads as work. Anchored to that bracketed glyph (it blinks between `!` and `.`) because the rest of the title is the person's own prompt, and a prompt that says `action required` must not read as a wait.
